prompt: How do I freeze panes in Excel?
completion:
**Freezing panes** keeps a row, column, or group of rows/columns visible while you scroll through the rest of the worksheet. Below are the simplest, most common ways to do it on the desktop versions of Excel (Windows & macOS). (Excel 365, 2019, 2016, 2013… all follow the same pattern.) --- ## 1. Freeze the Top Row or First Column | OS | Steps | |----|-------| | **Windows** | 1. Click the **View** tab.
2. In the **Window** group, click **Freeze Panes**.
3. Choose **Freeze Top Row** or **Freeze First Column**. | | **macOS** | 1. Click the **Layout** tab (or **View** in older versions).
2. Choose **Freeze Top Row** or **Freeze First Column** from the drop‑down. | **Tip:** - **Top Row** is great for headers that sit in row 1. - **First Column** is useful when you have a “key” column that you want to keep in view. --- ## 2. Freeze Panes at an Arbitrary Location This lets you freeze *any* combination of rows and columns. | OS | Steps | |----|-------| | **Windows** | 1. Click the cell *below* the rows you want frozen and *to the right* of the columns you want frozen.
(e.g., select **B2** to freeze row 1 and column A.)
2. Go to **View** → **Freeze Panes** → **Freeze Panes** (the plain option, not “Top Row”/“First Column”). | | **macOS** | 1. Click the desired cell (same rule: below the rows & right of the columns to freeze).
2. In the **Layout** tab, click **Freeze** → **Freeze Panes**. | **Example:** - If you want to keep rows 1–3 and columns A–C visible, select cell **D4** and freeze. --- ## 3. Unfreeze Panes | OS | Steps | |----|-------| | **Windows** | **View** → **Freeze Panes** → **Unfreeze Panes** | | **macOS** | **Layout** → **Freeze** → **Unfreeze Panes** | --- ## 4. Keyboard Shortcuts | OS | Shortcut | |----|----------| | **Windows** | `Alt` + `W`, `F`, `F` (Open Freeze Panes menu, then choose “Freeze Panes”) | | **macOS** | `Ctrl` + `Command` + `F` (directly toggles “Freeze Panes”) | *(The exact keys can vary slightly by Excel version; the menu navigation shortcut is reliable.)* --- ## 5. Common Pitfalls & Tips | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Nothing happens when I click “Freeze Panes”** | Make sure you’re *not* in the “View” tab’s “Page Layout” or “Page Break Preview.” The option works only in “Normal” view. | | **Freezing doesn’t work after opening a new workbook** | Each workbook has its own freeze settings. You must apply the freeze again in each sheet. | | **I can’t see the frozen area** | Check that you’re scrolling *after* the frozen rows/columns. If you scroll back to the top-left corner, the frozen area may appear hidden. | | **I accidentally froze too many rows** | Unfreeze, then repeat the freeze command but select a different cell. The new selection will determine which rows/columns stay visible. | | **Freeze panes in Excel Online?** | Excel for the web supports “Freeze Panes” but only in “Normal” view. The UI is a little different – look for the “Freeze Panes” button on the ribbon. | --- ### Quick Checklist 1. **Identify** which rows/columns you want frozen. 2. **Select** the cell *just below* and *just right of* the freeze zone. 3. **Apply** the appropriate Freeze option. 4. **Scroll** to confirm the freeze works. 5. **Unfreeze** when you’re done. That’s all there is to it! Happy spreadsheeting!
